### AccessOptions

```ts
type AccessOptions = Readonly<{
  defaultGrant?: Grant;
  grants?: Grants;
  required?: readonly string[];
  sessionGrants?: (context) => Grants;
  beforeCall?: (signal) => Promise<void>;
  confirmWrites?: boolean;
  approvedWrites?: (context) => readonly string[];
  confirm?: (request, signal) => Promise<boolean>;
  onRefused?: (refusal, context) => void;
}>;
```

Host-supplied access data and the one way to ask a person. Every field is
optional: hosted defaults allow unnamed modules, and no `confirm` means an
operation requiring approval is refused, never run unasked. MCP catalogs
explicitly default unnamed modules to none and require approval for writes.

### StandardOperationSchema

```ts
type StandardOperationSchema<T> = Readonly<{
  ~standard: Readonly<{
     validate: (value) =>
        | OperationSchemaResult<T>
       | Promise<OperationSchemaResult<T>>;
     jsonSchema: JsonSchemaSource["~standard"]["jsonSchema"];
  }>;
}>;
```

Any Standard Schema that also implements Standard JSON Schema, such as a Zod 4
schema. Mycelium validates with `validate` and describes the operation to the
model with `jsonSchema`.

### ToolAccessSchema

```ts
const ToolAccessSchema: Literals<readonly ["read", "write"]>;
```

What one operation does, declared by its author as a fixed fact: `read`
observes, `write` changes something. An unlabelled operation is `write`.

---

### ToolConfirmSchema

```ts
const ToolConfirmSchema: Boolean = Schema.Boolean;
```

Whether the author asks that a person approve each call first.

---

### ToolPolicySchema

```ts
const ToolPolicySchema: Struct<{
  access: optional<Literals<readonly ["read", "write"]>>;
  confirm: optional<Boolean>;
}>;
```

An author's labels for one operation or direct tool: the one definition both the
TypeScript type and the registration-time parse derive from.

---

### GrantSchema

```ts
const GrantSchema: Literals<readonly ["none", "read", "write"]>;
```

The access a host grants one module: `write` allows every operation, `read`
allows only `read` operations, `none` allows nothing.

---

Maximum number of out-of-band images retained for one execution.
